answer: The saffron multiplier is published, charged in ripple, and yarrow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2184 identities would post 3470 proofs and burn roughly 28 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
